contracts.title: Prior Information Notice - The Supply Of PROW Gates
contracts.description:
The purpose of this Prior Information Notice (PIN) is to initiate a market engagement exercise for the procurement of various designs of gates for the use of the Council's  Public Rights of Way team and to assess the interest and capability of the market to provide and deliver the Council's current and future requirements.  
      
      Worcestershire has around 16,000 individual public rights of way covering 4,600km.  This network, made up of footpaths, bridleways and byways, provides the public with a means of access on foot, horseback, cycle and, on a small number of routes, using motorised vehicles.  The network is used mostly for informal recreation but also in some locations, as important means of accessing shops, schools, places of employment and other services.
      
      Worcestershire County Council has the statutory responsibility to ensure that the County's Public Rights of Way network is properly mapped and maintained and the network is unobstructed and available for use by the public.  This responsibility is managed by the Public Rights of Way (PROW) Team, working with landowners and occupiers, volunteers, and appointed Service Providers. As part of this work we need to provide relevant Public Rights of Way gates to landowners. 
      
      Currently, Worcestershire County Council spends approximately £100,000 per year on gates. 
      
      The Market Engagement Questionnaire is available via Worcestershire County Council's e-procurement portal at: -   www.in-tendhost.co.uk/worcestershire

      • The current needs and outcomes of babies, infants, pre-school children and their families

      • Mapping of current provision and support for families with children aged 0-5
      • The views of local communities regarding their needs and experiences of support in early
      years
      • Local community assets in Worcestershire and how these can best be utilised to enhance

contracts.title: WORCESTERSHIRE COUNTY COUNCIL SUSTAINABILITY APPRAISAL OF THE WORCESTERSHIRE MINERALS LOCAL PLAN
contracts.description:
Worcestershire County Council is seeking to engage a single suitably qualified organisation to undertake a Sustainability Appraisal (SA), including Strategic Environmental Assessment, of the Worcestershire Minerals Local Plan fourth stage and any subsequent SA outputs necessary to support a sound Minerals Local Plan. The provider will work closely with the Council to ensure that a legally compliant SA is produced.
      
      WCC is preparing a new Minerals Local Plan for Worcestershire. This document will set out how we plan for mineral extraction in the county. It will guide how much and what minerals we need to be able to supply, where minerals should be extracted, how sites should be 'restored' when working has finished and how minerals development should protect and enhance Worcestershire's people and places. Once it is adopted it will replace the existing minerals policies in the Hereford and Worcester Minerals Local Plan and will be part of the Development Plan for Worcestershire, to be used to make decisions about planning applications for mineral extraction, processing and restoration in the county.
      
      The MLP is approaching its fourth stage of consultation. Each previous stage of the MLP was accompanied by an SA report produced in-house by WCC officers. Due to internal resource constraints, external consultants are being engaged to produce the SA of the MLP's fourth stage, and any subsequent SA input necessary to support a sound MLP. This also provides an opportunity for a 'critical friend' review to ensure that, as WCC approaches examination in public, the SA process to date can be demonstrated to be robust and legally compliant.

contracts.description:
Sustainable economic growth and business growth is a key priority for Worcestershire County Council, the district councils and the Worcestershire Local Enterprise Partnership. Set out in our corporate plan the Open for Business strategy focuses on ‘rebalancing’ Worcestershire's local economy through a series of measures aimed at encouraging and supporting private sector investment, business and employment growth. 

Central to the long term fortunes of the County are a large proportion of small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) which account for over 90% of all Worcestershire businesses and between them generate a high proportion of the County's Gross Value Added. Along with new businesses, those SMEs with the greatest potential for growth will play a significant role in the economic recovery of the County.

The County Council is seeking to appoint a service provider for the provision of business growth support as part of the Enterprising Worcestershire Programme through funding from the European Regional Development Fund, County and District Councils. 

The business growth support service will provide business advice and support to SMEs in Worcestershire in order to enable them to address barriers to business growth.
